flowPrompt.prompt:
GOOGLE FLOW (Veo 3.1) — VIDEO + AUDIO PROMPT
Duration: exactly 8 seconds · Aspect ratio: 9:16 vertical (1080×1920) · One continuous shot, no cuts.
Start frame: use the image generated from this video's Image Prompt (Frames to Video).

CONCEPT: Radio dishes across the globe link up as one Earth-sized telescope, and their combined view produced the first image of a black hole's shadow, in galaxy Messier 87, released in April 2019.
STYLE: Cinematic deep-space realism: scientifically grounded visuals, realistic planetary textures, volumetric nebula light, smooth majestic camera motion.
MAIN SUBJECT: A network of radio telescopes across Earth linked by glowing lines, and the resulting blurry orange ring around a dark shadow at the heart of galaxy Messier 87.
APPEARANCE: A network of radio telescopes across Earth linked by glowing lines, and the resulting blurry orange ring around a dark shadow at the heart of galaxy Messier 87
ENVIRONMENT & BACKGROUND: A high-altitude desert observatory at night, rising to a view of the whole Earth and the deep sky beyond.

TIMELINE (8.0 s total):
• 0.0–2.0 s — HOOK: A huge white radio dish on a high desert plateau tilts toward the night sky under steady stars.
• 2.0–6.0 s — MAIN ACTION: The camera rises from the dish into space, revealing points of light on several continents that link up with thin glowing lines across the globe, while a fuzzy orange ring with a dark center slowly forms in the black sky ahead.
• 6.0–8.0 s — PAYOFF & ENDING FRAME: The glowing orange ring around its dark shadow hangs in the darkness beyond the linked-up Earth. Hold the final composition steady for the last half second.

CAMERA: Low angle beside the dish, rising to orbit. Movement: Continuous drone rise into a wide space pull-back. Lens: 24 mm. Smooth, stabilized, cinematic motion; no shake, no sudden zooms.
LIGHTING & COLOR: Moonlit desert, glowing network lines and a warm orange ring glow. Color grade: Night blue, white and molten orange.
VISUAL EFFECTS: Illustrative glowing network lines between observatories and a soft blurry ring resembling the published image.
MOTION & PHYSICS: realistic physics and natural motion speed (not sped-up, not slow-motion unless stated). Camera and celestial motion are slow, smooth and majestic. Orbits, gas flows and particles follow believable physics.
CONSISTENCY: Celestial bodies keep the same size, color, texture and relative positions throughout. Background stars stay fixed and steady, with no twinkling flicker. The sense of scale stays vast and consistent.

AUDIO — generate together with the video, fully synchronized:
• Voice: Calm, deep Indian male documentary narrator with a subtle cinematic reverb. Language: Hindi (natural Hinglish, Indian accent). Tone: awe-struck, calm and mysterious. Pace: unhurried, about 2 words per second, crisp and clear pronunciation. The voice is the loudest audio layer.
• Voice-over (off-screen narrator — nobody on screen speaks, no lip movement):
   – 1.2–3.9 s — "दुनिया भर के telescopes एक साथ जुड़े…"
   – 4.2–7.4 s — "2019: black hole की छाया की पहली तस्वीर!"
• Background music: ORIGINAL instrumental score — triumphant, soaring orchestral finale with full brass, strings and timpani. No vocals, no lyrics, no humming; it must not imitate or resemble any existing song, artist or commercial melody. Mix the music about 25% quieter than the voice (roughly −18 dB under it) so every word stays clear. Gentle swell on the payoff around 6 s, then a natural fade-out from 7.0 s to 8.0 s.
• Sound effects (original, synchronized with the visuals):
   – 0.5 s — mechanical hum of the dish turning
   – 3.4 s — electric linking pulses
   – 6.2 s — deep triumphant boom
• Ambience: high desert night wind fading into a space hum; subtle and continuous under everything.
• Ending: all audio layers resolve and fade to silence by 8.0 s — no abrupt cut.

AVOID: no on-screen text, subtitles, captions or watermarks; no logos or brand names; no scene cuts, transitions or sudden scene changes; no flicker or frame-to-frame texture boiling; no camera shake or jitter; no morphing or melting shapes; no extra fingers, extra hands or extra limbs; no distorted anatomy; no face or identity changes between frames; no floating or disconnected objects; no broken physics; no unnatural or frozen expressions; no copyrighted or recognizable music, no song lyrics; no star flicker; no sudden scale jumps; no explosions unless described.
notes: In Flow, pick a Veo 3.x model that generates audio and set the aspect ratio to 9:16 before generating.
Flow generates about 8 seconds per clip, and this package is timed for exactly 8 seconds. Use Extend only if you deliberately want a 10-second version.
Best consistency: generate the image first, then use Frames to Video with that image as the start frame.
Hindi speech quality is not guaranteed by Veo. The voice is kept off-screen so there's no lip-sync to break. If pronunciation is poor, regenerate or record the line yourself.
If your Flow mode outputs silent video, don't add commercial music. Use an original track from YouTube Studio's Audio Library.
